title: What does LoanManage do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of LoanManage and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, LoanManage changes a loan's management state, including impairment, reversal of impairment or default where permitted. [1]

These are explicit lending lifecycle transitions rather than ordinary token payments. The permitted caller and current loan state constrain the operation. Inspect LoanID and the selected action carefully. An on-ledger default classification can affect accounting and cover, but it does not independently decide every legal remedy between lender and borrower. [1]

The LoanManage reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using LoanManage, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
